raw: {"status": "NO_PLAN", "reasons": ["The student's per-semester MC limit is 4, but all required courses (CS4211, CS2102, CS4212, CS2109S, CS3230, CS3211) are 4 MC each. With no other courses allowed to fill semesters (Rule 8), each course requires a full semester. However, prerequisites create a chain: CS2102 requires CS2030S/CS2040S (completed), CS3230 requires CS2040S (completed) and CS1231S (completed), CS3211 requires CS2106 or CG2271 (neither completed nor planned), CS4211 requires CS2103/CS2103T/CS2103DE/CS2113 (CS2103T completed), CS4212 requires CS2104 or CS3212 (neither completed nor planned), CS2109S requires CS2040S (completed) and Math (MA1521 completed). Crucially, CS3211 and CS4212 have unmet prerequisites (CS2106/CG2271 for CS3211; CS2104/CS3212 for CS4212) that are not in the 'must take' list and cannot be added as they are not prerequisites for the listed must-take courses (CS2102, CS3230, CS4211 do not require them). Thus, CS3211 and CS4212 cannot be taken.", "Even if prerequisites were met, the mutual exclusions and scheduling constraints make it impossible. CS3211 is Sem 2 only. CS4212 is Sem 2 only. CS4211 is Sem 1 only. CS2102 is Sem 1/2. CS3230 is Sem 1/2. CS2109S is Sem 1/2. The student is in Sem 4. Sem 4 is even (Sem 2 term). Sem 5 is odd (Sem 1 term). Sem 6 is even (Sem 2 term). Sem 7 is odd (Sem 1 term). Sem 8 is even (Sem 2 term). CS4211 (Sem 1) can only be in 5 or 7. CS3211 (Sem 2) can only be in 4, 6, 8. CS4212 (Sem 2) can only be in 4, 6, 8. The student wants CS3211 in Sem 6. CS4211 ideally before CS3230. CS2102 and CS2109S cannot be together. CS4211 and CS2102 cannot be together. With 4 MC limit, each course takes a whole semester. We have 6 courses. Semesters 4-8 are 5 semesters. 6 courses > 5 semesters. It is impossible to fit 6 courses into 5 semesters with a 4 MC limit if each course is 4 MC and no other courses can be added to share the load (Rule 8 forbids adding courses to fill semesters, but also implies we can't take 2 courses in one semester if they exceed 4 MC. Since each is 4 MC, we can only take 1 per semester). Therefore, 6 courses require 6 semesters. Only 5 semesters remain (4,5,6,7,8)."]
